chunks: We commanded man regarding his parents: his mother carried him in weakness upon weakness, and his weaning was in two years, saying: Be grateful to Me and to your parents. To Me is the journeying back.

key_terms.إِلَيَّ الْمَصِيرُ: To Me is the return/journeying back

ai.seo_question: What is the Quranic basis for gratitude towards parents and the specific mention of the mother's hardship?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse establishes the mother's primacy in parental rights due to the unique physical burdens of pregnancy and nursing, a concept further elaborated in hadiths that rank maternal service above paternal. The command to 'be grateful' (ishkur) extends beyond mere acknowledgment to active obedience and care, linking filial piety directly to one's ultimate accountability before Allah.
